- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) or neutral (0.0–0.4), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.8) but forecast rises sharply, check for overfitting; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.4–0.8), model often fails to mean-revert; force 3–5 day moving average alignment with true price path.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly bullish (≥0.8) and recent volatility is high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is rising, model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with bearish sentiment.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent false bullishness.
